name: Museo para la Identidad Nacional (MIN)
funding: Small foundation museum (930k visitors 2006-2019) run by the Fundación Hondureña para la Identidad Nacional; donors not published.
watch: The board was named in Nov 2022 to steer the museum through 'the greatest financial crisis' in its history. The sponsor block on its site is empty.
records_note: No reports or accounts found; nine unlabelled, undated logos show as pillar partners; the foundation board, appointed November 2022, is named in full.

name: Museo Ixchel del Traje Indígena
funding: Small private textile museum on the UFM campus; paid for by membership tiers (Q300 to Q10,000), the US charity Friends of the Ixchel Museum (since 1984) and project grants.
watch: Its 'current members' sponsor page names nobody. Past conservation grants came from Getty, Finland, the Carene Foundation and the US Embassy.
records_note: The museum publishes no reports, accounts, named donors or board; only its US friends charity files Form 990-EZ, 2009 to 2025.

name: Image Factory Art Foundation (Imagination Factory)
funding: Tiny artist-run non-profit since 1995; former PM Said Musa has given the North Front Street space free for 30 years. No other funders are published.
watch: Renamed Imagination Factory in 2025. Its website is a hosting placeholder. Founder Yasser Musa is Said Musa's son.
records_note: Its website is a coming-soon placeholder, so no reports, accounts, funders or board are published.

name: YARAT Contemporary Art Space
watch: Co-partnered a March 2026 exhibition with bp, SOCAR Midstream and PASHA Holding; funder roster itself not published.
records_note: No reports or accounts found; the partners page shows eight unnamed, undated logos, and the team page lists staff but no board.
other_findings: WikiLeaks, 2010-01: An embassy profile of the First Lady's Pashayev family: it controls PASHA Holding and runs the Heydar Aliyev Foundation. YARAT's founder is the First Lady's niece, and PASHA Holding co-partnered a 2026 YARAT show. (Cablegate 10BAKU54)

name: Heydar Aliyev Center
funding: A US$250M Azerbaijani state project opened in 2012; its main contractor was tied to the Aliyev family's offshore network.
watch: Zaha Hadid building named for Heydar Aliyev; site cleared by forced evictions Zaha Hadid building named for Heydar Aliyev; site cleared by forced evictions
records_note: The centre's site carries no annual reports, accounts, sponsor list or board; it publishes only a statute and structure page for this state body.

name: Armenian Center for Contemporary Experimental Art (ACCEA/NPAK)
funding: Small diaspora-funded NGO (US 501(c)(3) since 1995) with benefactors incl. Balassanian, Cafesjian, Boghossian, Hovnanian funds; state gives building free since 2002.
watch: Founded 1992 by the Balassanians; 2022 benefactor list: diaspora family funds and Boghossian (jewellery) Founded 1992 by the Balassanians; 2022 benefactor list: diaspora family funds and Boghossian (jewellery)
records_note: Its site posts no reports; it lists major benefactors as of February 2022 and its board, and its US arm files Form 990-EZ.

name: Modern Art Museum of Yerevan
funding: Small museum founded in 1972 with the city's backing and listed among Yerevan municipality's museums; its current funder roster is not published.
watch: First Soviet museum devoted to modern art; director Nune Avetisyan First Soviet museum devoted to modern art; director Nune Avetisyan
records_note: No annual reports, accounts, funder list or board found on the museum site; the team page lists the director and staff only.

name: Tbilisi Photography & Multimedia Museum (TPMM)
funding: Small NGO museum (founded 2017) in Stamba Hotel; funded by Swiss SDC, Adjara Group/Stamba, Prince Claus Fund, OSGF, MG Law, MagiC Carpets.
watch: Moved some operations to a Lithuanian NGO after Georgia's 2024 foreign-agent law Moved some operations to a Lithuanian NGO after Georgia's 2024 foreign-agent law
records_note: No annual reports or accounts found; a Donors and Partners footer block shows seven named-in-alt logos with no date, and no board is listed.

name: State Museum of Arts of the Republic of Karakalpakstan (Savitsky Museum)
funding: State museum with about 70,000 visitors in 2025; the government-backed ACDF paid for its renovation, restorers and digitisation.
watch: Savitsky's collection of banned Soviet avant-garde art; refurbished by the state ACDF Savitsky's collection of banned Soviet avant-garde art; refurbished by the state ACDF
records_note: The museum site has no annual reports, accounts or funder list; it names the director and a deputy for finance but no board.

name: A. Kasteyev State Museum of Arts
watch: Now styled the Abilkhan Kasteev National Museum of Art; 2021 noise dispute with Esentai luxury housing Now styled the Abilkhan Kasteev National Museum of Art; 2021 noise dispute with Esentai luxury housing
records_note: Its old site posted narrative annual reports for 2017 to 2019 without accounts; the new site was unreadable.

name: Gapar Aitiev Kyrgyz National Museum of Fine Arts
watch: In December 2019 a Culture Ministry commission confiscated works from the Feminnale; director Mira Dzhangaracheva left after death threats. Permanent display closed for repairs from late Sept 2025
why_flagged: Underfunded national museum (about 18,000 works) paid for by Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Culture; no sponsor roster published.
records_note: A state museum; its site has no reports, accounts, donor list or board, and a search found none from the ministry.

name: Savannah Centre for Contemporary Art (SCCA Tamale)
records_note: No reports, accounts or funder list found; the site lists individuals who collaborated and supported it, in no order or date, and names no board.
